general.description: Chemosynthetic and thermosynthetic extremophile organisms that grow on fumaroles and volcanic vents. They derive energy from geothermal activity and often incorporate mineral deposits from vent ejecta, giving them semi-inorganic appearances.
environmental_context: Found directly on fumaroles and gas vent structures
Often appear in clusters on flat volcanic terrain
Require active geothermal heat sources to sustain metabolism

color_variants.rule: Color depends on rare planetary materials (NOT star type in canon behavior, but can be normalized if needed)

Fumerola aquatis.description: Water-volcanism adapted variant forming dark clustered folds that trap geothermal heat.

Fumerola carbosis.description: Thin tubular structures adapted to carbon and methane volcanic emissions.

Fumerola extremus.description: Highly adaptive variant found on silicate, iron, and rocky volcanism zones. Exhibits strong environmental plasticity.

Fumerola nitris.description: Ovoid nitrogen-based variant with dotted surface markings, optimized for nitrogen/ammonia vents.

special_rules: Fumarole geological feature is mandatory spawn condition
Volcanism type is the primary species driver
Color is determined by local rare materials, not star class
Minimum sample distance is 100m due to dense clustering
All species are strongly dependent on active geothermal activity
